records.label: Large consanguineous Turkish family

phenotypes.hpo_label: Cerebellar ataxia associated with quadrupedal gait

phenotypes.text: atrophy of superior, middle, and inferior cerebellar peduncles
morphometric abnormalities of precentral gyrus and Brodmann areas BA6, BA44, BA45

records.segregation: Cosegregated with the condition in the extended family; obligate carriers heterozygous
quotes: We investigated a large consanguineous family from Turkey exhibiting an extremely rare phenotype associated with quadrupedal locomotion, mental retardation, and cerebro-cerebellar hypoplasia, linked to a 7.1-Mb region of homozygosity on chromosome 17p13.1-13.3.

Targeted sequencing of the entire homozygous region in three affected individuals and two obligate carriers uncovered a private missense mutation, WDR81 p.P856L, which cosegregated with the condition in the extended family.

Diffusion weighted imaging and fiber tractography of the patients' brains revealed morphological abnormalities in the cerebellum and corpus callosum, in particular atrophy of superior, middle, and inferior peduncles of the cerebellum.

records.label: Consanguineous Turkish family

phenotypes.hpo_label: Cerebellar ataxia associated with quadrupedal gait

records.segregation: segregation analysis supported the variant; it lies in a shared homozygous region on 13q12
quotes: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
Missense mutation in the ATPase, aminophospholipid transporter protein ATP8A2 is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.

records.label: IV.4 (proband)

phenotypes.text: inability to walk, sit, or hold head; wheelchair-bound

records.segregation: Homozygous in 3 affected sibs; heterozygous in both parents and 2 healthy sibs; wild type in 1 healthy sib
quotes: The proband (Ⅳ. 4) was a 9‐year‐old girl from healthy and first‐cousin parents with Arab descent (Figure 1A).

The first noticeable clinical sign was severe neonatal hypotonia. Afterward, she demonstrated a lag in all psychomotor and developmental milestones. In the aspect of motor performance assessment, she was wheelchair‐bound and could not walk, sit, or hold her head.

According to segregation analysis, the sequence variant was homozygous in the affected individuals (Ⅳ0.1, Ⅳ0.2, Ⅳ0.4) (Figure 1C) and heterozygous in the parents (Ⅲ. 1, Ⅲ. 2), one healthy brother (Ⅳ. 3), and one healthy sister (Ⅳ. 5) (Figure 1D).

records.label: Affected sibs IV.1 and IV.2
records.segregation: Homozygous in affected sibs; parents heterozygous
quotes: Index case has five siblings: two healthy sisters (Ⅳ. 5, Ⅳ. 6), one healthy brother (Ⅳ. 3), one affected sister (Ⅳ. 2), and one affected brother (Ⅳ. 1). Patients Ⅳ. 1 and Ⅳ. 2 were 17 and 15 years old with phenotypical characteristics similar to those present in the proband.

All 3 patients had limited intellectual functioning with IQ levels ranging from 20 to 40. Also, they had delayed speech and language as well as signs of dysarthria. Nevertheless, the hearing examination of patients was not shown any significant impairment.
In these patients, deep tendon reflexes were absent.

records.label: Two siblings

phenotypes.text: delayed independent gait, acquired by age 4 years

quotes: we describe two siblings with congenital ataxia, who acquired independent gait by age 4 years. After 16 years of follow-up they presented near normal cognition, cerebellar ataxia, mild pyramidal signs, and dystonia.
On exome sequencing, a novel homozygous variant (c.1580-18C > G - intron 17) in ATP8A2 was identified.

records.label: Japanese siblings
quotes: Japanese siblings presented with athetotic movements at 1 and 2 months of age. They also had ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, feeding difficulty, hypotonia, and severely delayed development. One patient had retinal degeneration and optic atrophy.
Flattening of the auditory brainstem responses and areflexia developed. At the last follow-up, neither patient could sit or achieve head control, although some nonverbal communication was preserved.
Whole exome sequencing revealed compound heterozygous variants of ATP8A2: NM_016529.6:c.[1741C>T];[2158C>T] p.[(Arg581*)];[(Arg720*)].

notes.statement: Narishige et al. (2022) noted that because the symptoms of CAMRQ4 did not progress early in development, the disorder was difficult to distinguish from dyskinetic cerebral palsy, especially in solitary cases, but suggested that visual and hearing impairments together with involuntary movements and severe developmental delay may be a clue to suspect CAMRQ4.
quotes: The symptoms did not progress in the early period of development, which makes it difficult to distinguish from dyskinetic cerebral palsy, particularly in solitary cases.
However, visual and hearing impairments associated with involuntary movements and severe developmental delay may be a clue to suspect CAMRQ4.

notes.statement: Damásio et al. (2021) showed in a minigene assay in HEK293T cells that the ATP8A2 c.1580-18C-G variant produced an aberrant transcript that kept 17 bp of intron 17 because an alternative acceptor splice site was used. This inserted four amino acids and led to a premature stop codon. The authors concluded that the variant causes disease.
quotes: The construct with the c.1580-18C > G homozygous variant produced an aberrant transcript, leading to retention of 17 bp of intron 17, by the use of an alternative acceptor splice site, resulting in a premature stop codon by insertion of four amino acids.

notes.statement: Damásio et al. (2021) concluded that their findings expand the ATP8A2-related disorders to include less severe forms of congenital ataxia.
quotes: These results allowed us to establish this as a disease-causing variant and expand ATP8A2-related disorders to include less severe forms of congenital ataxia.

notes.statement: Mohamadian et al. (2020) found that the ATP8A2 p.Gly447Arg variant was absent from public databases and from 100 ethnically matched controls, and classified it as likely pathogenic by ACMG criteria. Glycine-447 lies in a highly conserved subregion of the cytoplasmic N (ATP-binding) domain.
quotes: The identified novel variant was not found in 100 healthy and ethnically matched controls.
According to the American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guideline, the sequence variant c.1339G > A in ATP8A2 classified as “likely pathogenic”
glycine 447 is located within an extremely conserved subregion of cytoplasmic domain N, known as ATP‐binding domain.

notes.statement: Mohamadian et al. (2020) used homology modeling to predict that the G447R substitution greatly reduced the stability of the ATP8A2 protein and changed the ligand-binding pocket, which they suggested may lower ligand-binding affinity and catalytic activity.
quotes: About the FoldX algorithm prediction, the substitution of Glycine to Arginine at position 447 results in a severely reduced protein stability with ddG of 7.94 kcal/mol.
According to 3DLigandSite output, the amino acid residue 447 is adjacent to the active site, and mutation p.G447R affected the ligand‐binding pocket.
It may dramatically decrease the ligand‐binding affinity, ligand specificity, and the catalytic activity of ATP8A2.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) used homozygosity mapping in a consanguineous Turkish family with 4 affected individuals and found several shared homozygous regions, including one on chromosome 13q12.
quotes: Homozygosity mapping revealed that several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) reported that the ATP8A2 I376M variant lies in a highly conserved C-terminal transmembrane region of the E1-E2 ATPase domain.
quotes: The mutation lies in a highly conserved C-terminal transmembrane region of E1 E2 ATPase domain.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) noted that ATP8A2 is expressed mainly in the brain and during development, particularly in the cerebellum.
quotes: The ATP8A2 gene is mainly expressed in brain and development, in particular cerebellum.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) noted that ATP8A2 had been disrupted by a de novo balanced t(10;13) translocation in an unrelated individual with mental retardation and severe hypotonia.
quotes: Interestingly, an unrelated individual has been identified, in whom mental retardation and severe hypotonia is associated with a de novo t(10;13) balanced translocation resulting with the disruption of ATP8A2.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) suggested that ATP8A2 is involved in the development of the cerebro-cerebellar structures that humans need for posture and gait.
quotes: These findings suggest that ATP8A2 is involved in the development of the cerebro-cerebellar structures required for posture and gait in humans.

notes.statement: Onat et al. (2013) described cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation, and dysequilibrium syndrome as a rare and heterogeneous condition.
quotes: Cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequilibrium syndrome is a rare and heterogeneous condition.

notes.statement: Gulsuner et al. (2011) linked the disorder in a large consanguineous Turkish family to a 7.1-Mb region of homozygosity on chromosome 17p13.1-p13.3.
quotes: linked to a 7.1-Mb region of homozygosity on chromosome 17p13.1-13.3

notes.statement: Gulsuner et al. (2011) reported that the P856L mutation lies in a highly conserved region of WDR81, between an N-terminal BEACH domain and C-terminal WD40 beta-propeller domains. WDR81 was predicted to be a transmembrane protein and was highly expressed in the cerebellum and corpus callosum, especially in the Purkinje cell layer.
quotes: The mutation lies in a highly conserved region of WDR81, flanked by an N-terminal BEACH domain and C-terminal WD40 beta-propeller domains. WDR81 is predicted to be a transmembrane protein.
It is highly expressed in the cerebellum and corpus callosum, in particular in the Purkinje cell layer of the cerebellum.

notes.statement: Gulsuner et al. (2011) stated that WDR81 was the third gene implicated in quadrupedal locomotion in humans, after VLDLR and CA8.
quotes: WDR81 represents the third gene, after VLDLR and CA8, implicated in quadrupedal locomotion in humans.

notes.statement: In a reply to Herz et al. and Humphrey et al., Ozcelik et al. (2008) addressed the genetic heterogeneity of cerebellar hypoplasia with quadrupedal locomotion.
quotes: Reply to Herz et al. and Humphrey et al.: Genetic heterogeneity of cerebellar hypoplasia with quadrupedal locomotion.

notes.statement: Ozcelik et al. (2008) studied 4 large consanguineous Turkish kindreds with quadrupedal gait (Unertan syndrome). In families A and D the trait mapped to chromosome 9p24, and they found VLDLR mutations: R257X in family A and c2339delT in family D. In families B and C the phenotype was not linked to chromosome 9p. From this the authors concluded that hereditary disorders associated with quadrupedal gait in humans are genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: Four large consanguineous kindreds from Turkey manifest this phenotype.
In two other families (B and C), the phenotype is not linked to chromosome 9p.
hereditary disorders associated with quadrupedal gait in humans are genetically heterogeneous

notes.statement: Ozcelik et al. (2008) described quadrupedal gait in humans (Unertan syndrome) as a rare phenotype associated with dysarthric speech, mental retardation, and varying degrees of cerebrocerebellar hypoplasia.
quotes: Quadrupedal gait in humans, also known as Unertan syndrome, is a rare phenotype associated with dysarthric speech, mental retardation, and varying degrees of cerebrocerebellar hypoplasia.
